items.q: What does a site actually cost?
items.a: Ready-made sites carry their price on the listing. Custom builds are quoted per project — a one-page site for a small business sits at the low end, a multi-page site with booking, a catalogue or online payments sits higher. You get one fixed number before anything starts, and it doesn't move unless you add pages.

A ready-made site can be on your domain within a few days — most of that time is you sending text and photos. A custom build depends on how many pages there are; you'll get a specific completion date with the quote, not a range.

Design, build, mobile layout, the three-language setup if you want it, basic search-engine setup, and putting it live on your domain. Domain registration and hosting fees are paid to those providers directly — I'll tell you exactly what they cost before you commit, and I never mark them up.

items.q: How many changes can I ask for?
items.a: Two full rounds of revisions are included after the first working version. That's the point where most sites land. Beyond that, changes are billed by the hour at a rate I'll tell you up front, and small fixes — a wrong phone number, a typo — are always free.

items.q: How do I pay, and is it safe?
items.a: You transfer the amount from whichever banking or e-wallet app you already use, to the card or IBAN shown at checkout, with your order reference in the description. Then you upload the receipt. This site never sees your card number, your CVV or your bank login — there is no field for them anywhere. For custom orders you can split it: a deposit to start, the rest when the site is finished and you've seen it working.

items.q: What if I pay and don't get what I asked for?
items.a: Read the refund policy in full — it's linked in the footer and it's short. In brief: before I start work, a deposit is fully refundable. After delivery, if the site doesn't do what the quote said it would, I fix it or refund it. What isn't refundable is changing your mind about a finished, delivered site that matches its brief.

items.q: Can the site be in Azerbaijani, Russian and English?
items.a: Yes, and it's the normal case here rather than an add-on — this site itself runs in all three. If you supply text in one language only, I'll tell you what translation will cost before adding it.

items.q: Who owns the site when it's done?
items.a: You do — the domain, the hosting account, the code and the content are all registered in your name and handed over. You are not renting anything from me and you don't need me to make changes later. If you want me to keep maintaining it, that's a separate arrangement you can end at any time.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: These terms cover what you get when you order a site through WebSale.az and what is expected from both sides. They're written to be read, not to be survived.

sections.b: WebSale.az is run by one person based in Baku, Azerbaijan. There is no agency behind it. When you send a message, that person reads it. Contact details are in the footer of every page.

A listing shows the finished site, its price and its licence before you buy. Buying one gets you the source code, setup on your domain, and your own text, photos and logo put in place. The licence covers one business on one domain — you can modify the site however you like, but you can't resell it as a template.

You send a request, you get back a fixed price, a written scope of what's included and a completion date. Nothing starts until you accept. If you later want something outside that scope, it gets quoted separately rather than absorbed silently or dropped.

Two full rounds of changes are included after the first working version, for both ready-made and custom sites. Fixing something that doesn't match the agreed scope isn't a revision round — that's just finishing the job, and it's free.

Payment is by bank transfer or e-wallet to the account shown at checkout, with your order reference in the description. Your payment is confirmed once it appears in the receiving bank statement — not when you upload the receipt. This site never asks for, receives or stores your card number, expiry date, CVV or bank login.

Text, photos, logo and any accounts the site needs to connect to. If those don't arrive, the completion date moves by however long it takes them to. Anything you send has to be yours to send — if you supply photos or text you don't own the rights to, that's on you.

Once the final payment is confirmed, the site is yours: domain, hosting account, code and content, all in your name. There is no ongoing licence fee and you don't need permission to change it or to have someone else work on it.

Hosting and domain fees are paid to those providers directly at their prices. Ongoing maintenance, new features after handover, and content updates are separate work. Search-engine rankings, sales figures and traffic levels are not something anyone can promise, and are not promised here.

You can cancel a custom build at any time before delivery. What happens to money already paid is set out in the refund policy. If you become impossible to reach for 60 days mid-build, the order is paused and, after that, closed with the refund policy applied.
These terms are governed by the law of the Republic of Azerbaijan. If something goes wrong, email first — nearly everything is fixable that way.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: What this site collects, why, and what happens to it. Short, because it doesn't collect much.

sections.b: Your name and email when you create an account. Whatever you write in a site request. Your order history. Payment receipts you choose to upload. If you sign in with Google or Microsoft, they give this site your name, email and profile picture — nothing else, and no access to your files or mail.
Card numbers, expiry dates, CVV codes, bank logins. There is no form field for any of these anywhere on this site, because payments happen inside your own banking app and never pass through here.

To quote your project, build it, keep you updated, confirm payments, and keep the accounting records that tax law requires. That's the whole list. Nothing is sold to anyone and there is no advertising network embedded on this site.
Account details, orders and uploaded receipts are stored with Supabase, the database and file-storage provider behind this site. Receipt files are private: only you and the site owner can open them.

Your account data stays until you delete your account. Completed orders and their receipts are kept for as long as accounting law requires them, which is why deleting your account doesn't erase those.
Two things are stored in your browser: your sign-in session, and your language choice. There are no tracking or advertising cookies, and therefore no cookie banner to click through.
You can see and edit your details on your profile page, delete your account, or email and ask for a copy of everything held about you. Requests like that are answered within 30 days.

refund.title: Refund & dispute policy
refund.intro: Payments here go directly between your bank and mine, so there's no card processor to arbitrate. That makes it more important, not less, that the rules are written down plainly in advance. This is the whole policy.

sections.b: A deposit is fully refundable at any point before I begin building. Say the word and it goes back the way it came, within five working days.

sections.h: While the site is being built
sections.b: If you cancel mid-build, you pay for the work already done and the rest is returned. You get an itemised note of what that covers — no round numbers pulled out of the air — and you keep whatever has been built so far.

If the delivered site doesn't do what the accepted quote said it would, I fix it. If it can't be fixed, you get a full refund and keep nothing that was delivered. If it does match the quote and you've simply changed your mind, that isn't refundable — the work exists and it was done to your brief.

You can see the full working demo before you pay, so there's no hidden surprise. Once the code and logins have been handed to you, the sale is final. If handover hasn't happened yet, you get a full refund on request.

Transfers without the order reference are the usual problem — they're slow to trace, not lost. Send me the receipt and the exact time of the transfer and I'll find it. If you paid twice, the duplicate goes back within five working days.

Email first, always: describe the problem and what would fix it. I aim to reply within two working days and to settle it within ten. If we genuinely can't agree, either side can take it to the courts of the Republic of Azerbaijan — but in a business this size, that helps nobody, and it has never been necessary.
To the same account the money came from, in AZN, within five working days of being agreed. Any transfer fee charged by your own bank is theirs, not mine, and I can't refund it.
